runs: Choose which runs and references appear in every chart. References only apply to the nowcast charts.
lossscale: Raw shows the loss as logged. Relative divides each run's loss by its own starting loss (start) or by base Chronos-2 on the same blocks (base). The x axis is simulations trained, from each run's own checkpoints and logged chunks, so runs with different steps per simulation line up. Full range (the default) shows every run whole; live run zooms to the current run.
train: Quantile (pinball) loss on the training batches, as a rolling mean of 20 logged points. Lower is better. Faint dots are the live run's single logged values. Run colours are in the selector at the top.
held: The same loss on the validation simulations (the grid's validation round), which the model never trains on. Lower is better. The line is the monitor on the first 100 validation blocks at each evaluation (subset); the points are the full validation set at each checkpoint, with step 0 at zero simulations. Dashed lines and triangles are the part of the loss on the nowcast steps, from the start of each block's window to its cut-off; dotted lines and squares the part on the forecast steps after it. The parts sum to the loss. The trainer logs no subset loss at step 0, so relative to start divides the subset by its first evaluation, and relative to base Chronos-2 shows the full set only.
losstype: Which validation loss the validation panel shows, for every selected run: total; the nowcast steps (from the start of each block's window to its cut-off) or the forecast steps after it; by data layout; or by level (national, intermediate, leaf). Lines are the subset monitor at each evaluation, points the full set at step 0 and each checkpoint. By layout and by level, colour is the layout or level and line style the run. Level losses exist at step 0 and at checkpoints only.
bysrc: Validation loss split by data layout, at each validation evaluation from step 0 (zero-shot). Colour is the layout and line style is the run.
biasline: Each relation's 144 values (12 layers x 12 heads) against simulations trained: the line is their mean, the band their min to max. One panel per relation, all on one scale; every selected run is drawn, its line style in the legend. Each run's values are its own: its history, its logged means and ranges, and its checkpoints' adapters; a run with none is listed as missing.
biasheat: One square per layer (row) x head (column), the latest saved values of the run named above the panels, on one scale for every relation (the key above). Orange means that head attends more than base Chronos-2 to that kind of pair, blue less. A bias of 1 weights those pairs x2.7.
relations: same = a place's counts, lags and totals. up = a place to its country. down = a country to its places. self = a row with itself, shown only for runs that train it.
lr: Learning rate of each optimiser group. Each run is drawn against simulations trained: the rate falls linearly to zero at the run's last simulation. The dot marks where the run is now.
perf: WIS or CRPS relative to randomwalknowcast. Below 1 is better. One line per run across checkpoints, with the zero-shot and randomwalknowcast references.
nowcast: One nowcast date: the median and 50% and 90% bands of each ticked run for the chosen date, against the truth (95% where the forecasts stop at the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles, as the German hub's do); line style runs from dotted (earliest checkpoint) to solid (latest). Nowcasts over time: one model's nowcasts from several origins on one plot, each with its horizons, against the final truth (the latest release where there is one), as in the paper's nowcasts-over-time panel. The slider and buttons move the latest origin; Origins and every set how many and how far apart.
wis: Mean score over the nowcast dates the ticked runs have in common: weighted interval score for quantile forecasts, sample CRPS for sample forecasts. Lower is better. Each WIS bar is split into dispersion (interval width), overprediction (truth below the intervals) and underprediction (truth above), shades of the row's colour as in the paper; hover a part for its value.
logwis: The same WIS on the log scale: of log(x + 1) of the truth and of each quantile, as the shared scorer takes log WIS. It weighs relative errors, so small and large counts count alike. Split into the same three parts.
coverage: Share of truths inside the 50% and 90% intervals, as in the paper. The 90% interval needs the 5% and 95% quantiles: sample-based datasets give them, but the German hub's quantiles stop at 2.5% and 97.5%, so German rows use the 95% interval. The dashed lines mark the nominal levels.
biasscore: Mean of 1 minus 2 times the forecast CDF at the truth, from -1 (forecast too low) to +1 (too high). 0 is unbiased.
t_step: The trainer's current optimiser step and simulations trained, from its status file.
t_rate: Training speed from the trainer's timestamped steps: each logged step and its status file, which it writes every few steps. Over the last hour, or the last two points if they are further apart (evaluations log a step only every few hundred). Since the last restart only. Below: the mean over the whole run (leaving out stops of over half an hour).
t_next: Simulations trained so far of the next checkpoint's size, and when it is due: the simulations still to go at the run's steps a simulation so far, at the steps a second since the last restart. A checkpoint already written and still being scored at its size is named below with the time it was written.
t_eta: Time to the final checkpoint, worked out as for the next checkpoint.
t_lr: Current learning rate of each optimiser group.
t_trainer: Whether the trainer process is running.
t_log: Time of the last training log line. It turns red after 10 minutes.
lorabylayer: How far the LoRA adapter has moved each encoder layer from base Chronos-2: the Frobenius norm of the scaled update B·A, a layer's time and group attention modules added in quadrature. One line per run, at its last checkpoint, in the run's colour. It shows where the model changes, not whether it improves: expect steady growth that slows as the learning rate falls, with no one layer running away.
lorabykind: The same update size split by kind of module: time attention (along each series), group attention (across the series of a block) and the output layer, at each checkpoint against simulations trained; colour is the kind, line style the run. Growing group attention means the model is learning how places relate; growth that levels off late in the run is expected as the learning rate falls to zero.
wissplit: Each model's mean WIS over the common nowcast dates, as the other score panels, split by the part of the horizon: the nowcast part, reference dates up to the nowcast date (solid), and the forecast part, reference dates after it, by week ahead (cross-hatched). The same split as the validation loss and the paper. A dataset whose targets end at the nowcast date (the German hub's, 28 days back to the nowcast date) has no forecast part.
t_tput: Throughput from the trainer's chunk-time lines: each finished chunk's waiting for batches, cutting blocks, training and evaluating time. Steps and simulations over that time only, so a restart or a pause between chunks does not count. GPU busy is the share spent training and evaluating; waiting and cutting run on the CPU. This segment is the running segment's log; whole run is every segment's, a chunk logged twice counted once.
t_now: What the trainer is doing now, from its status file: its stage and, while a chunk trains, that chunk's simulations, the steps done of it (the step less the steps of the chunks already finished) and the time left at the current steps a second.
t_timings: Each checkpoint's segment from the trainer's chunk-time lines: its chunks, steps, and time spent training, cutting blocks and evaluating (the checkpoint's own evaluation is in its last chunk). In all is the chunks' own time, not wall time: saves and restarts between chunks are left out. A segment with no saved checkpoint yet is marked running.
